# Harness Execution Summary

The candidate exhibits critical **systematic label bias** across all three datasets. On ds_alpha, eval accuracy reaches only 39.6%; on ds_beta it drops to 25%; on ds_gamma, performance is similarly poor. 

The dominant failure pattern is **mode collapse**: the model repeatedly predicts a single label regardless of input—"dorxo-hako" on alpha, "bragro-dorsto" on beta, and "grozi-brapi" on gamma—suggesting the demonstrations are failing to establish meaningful decision boundaries. This indicates the in-context examples are either poorly representative of the label space or insufficiently diverse to prevent the model from defaulting to surface-level pattern matching. 

Training accuracy lags far behind eval accuracy (22.6% vs 39.6% on alpha; 34.7% vs 25% on beta), revealing instability in the learning process rather than stable generalization. The relatively small context windows (341–515 chars) may also be constraining the model's ability to leverage richer contextual signals. To improve, focus on diversifying and reweighting demonstrations to cover underrepresented labels and ensure each label appears with sufficient contextual variation in the in-context examples.
